sentences.zh: 治平三年，翰林學士賈黯奏：“近者皇子封拜，並除檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Zhiping era, Hanlin Academician Jia Yan memorialized: “Recently, when imperial sons were enfeoffed, all were concurrently appointed Acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiping 3, Hanlin academician Jia Yan submitted: “Lately, whenever imperial sons were enfeoffed, they were all given the provisional title Grand Tutor as well.

sentences.zh: 臣按官儀，自後魏以來，以太師、太傅、太保為三師，太尉、司徒、司空為三公，國朝因之。

translations.literal: Your servant has reviewed the statutes on offices: since the Later Wei, Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Guardian have been the Three Preceptors, and Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works the Three Excellencies; our dynasty follows this.
translations.idiomatic: I have checked the office regulations: since the Later Wei, the Three Preceptors have been Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Guardian, and the Three Excellencies Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works; the Song continues that arrangement.

translations.literal: The Six Offices Canon states: ‘The Three Preceptors are officers for instruction and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Offices Canon says, ‘The Three Preceptors are officers of instruction and guidance.

translations.literal: ’They are those whom the Son of Heaven takes as his models and teachers.
translations.idiomatic: They are the men whom the Son of Heaven takes as his teachers and models.

sentences.zh: 今皇太子以師傅名官，於義弗安，莫甚於此，蓋前世因循，失於厘正。

translations.literal: Now the Crown Prince uses the names Preceptor and Tutor as his official titles; in ritual propriety nothing is more ill-fitting than this—it is a legacy of past dynasties carried on through inertia, a failure to correct what was amiss.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the heir apparent now bears offices called Preceptor and Tutor; nothing offends ritual logic more sharply. It is sheer inertia from earlier ages—a correction long overdue.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以謂自今皇子及宗室卑者除官，並不可帶師傅之名，隨其敘遷改授三公之官。”

translations.literal: Your servant considers that from this point forward, whenever imperial sons and members of the imperial clan of lower standing receive offices, none should bear the names Preceptor or Tutor; according to their seniority in rank they should instead be given offices among the Three Excellencies.”
translations.idiomatic: I humbly propose that hereafter, when imperial sons and junior members of the clan are appointed, none should carry the titles Preceptor or Tutor; let promotions follow seniority into offices among the Three Excellencies instead.

translations.literal: An edict responded: “Wait for the future, and then correct it accordingly.”
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: “We shall wait for a suitable occasion and revise the practice then."

sentences.zh: 自此，皇子及宗室卑行，遂不除三師官。

translations.literal: Thereafter imperial sons and junior lines of the imperial clan were no longer appointed to the Three Preceptors.
translations.idiomatic: After that, imperial sons and junior clansmen were no longer given the Three Preceptors.

sentences.zh: 宋初，台、省、寺、監官猶多蒞本司，亦各有員額資考之製，各以曹署閑劇著為月限，考滿則遷，慶恩止轉階、勳、爵、邑。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song, officials of the provincial bureaus, ministries, directorates, and supervisory offices still largely attended in their home offices; each also had fixed quotas and regulations for merit review; each bureau's relative workload was set as a monthly schedule; when review was complete one transferred; at celebratory amnesties only rank steps, merit orders, enfeoffments, and fiefs were advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, officials of the commissions, ministries, directorates, and supervisory agencies still largely served in their home offices, each with fixed quotas and merit-review rules; every agency's workload set the monthly term, and when review ended came promotion—while amnesties advanced only rank, honors, titles, and fiefs.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，始以右監門衛將軍魏仁滌為右神武將軍，水部員外郎朱洞為都官員外郎，監察御史李鑄為殿中侍御史，以仁滌等掌麹蘖、領關征外有羨也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, for the first time Right Supervisor of the Gate Guards Wei Rendì was made Right Divine Tiger General, Water Ministry Junior Director Zhu Dong was made Capital Investigation Junior Director, and Supervising Censor Li Zhu was made Attending Palace Censor—because Rendì and the others supervised yeast mash and collected transit duties, with surplus revenue beyond the norm.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 2, Wei Rendì of the Right Gate Guard was first made Right Divine Tiger General, Zhu Dong of the Water Ministry a Capital Investigation junior director, and Li Zhu a palace attending censor—since they managed distillery duties and frontier transit levies with profits beyond quota.

translations.literal: From this time forward, the statute on annual completion and ranked promotion was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the rule of promotion upon completing the annual term was discarded.

sentences.zh: 是後，多掌事於外，諸司互以他官領之，雖有正官，非別受詔亦不領本司之務。

translations.literal: Afterward most duties were handled outside [the capital]; the various agencies frequently had other officials lead them; even when there was a proper incumbent, unless he separately received an edict he did not preside over his home office's business.
translations.idiomatic: Later most business was conducted on assignment away from the capital; agencies were commonly headed by outsiders; even nominal incumbents did not run their home offices without a specific edict.

sentences.zh: 又官有其名而不除者甚眾，皆無定員、無月限，不計資品，任官者但常食其奉而已。

translations.literal: Moreover, many offices had names but no appointees; all lacked fixed quotas and monthly terms, and rank grades were not counted; those who held office merely drew their salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Many offices existed in name only; without fixed quotas or monthly terms, rank ceased to matter, and appointees merely collected salary.

sentences.zh: 時議以近職為貴，中外又以差遣別輕重焉。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion held posts near the throne most honorable; within and outside the court, commissioned duties also divided heavy from light.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion prized service close to the throne; inside and outside the court, temporary assignments likewise sorted prestige.

translations.literal: Above: on the civil prestige-rank tier, one step was added on grace; on the Gentleman tier, capital and court officials received five steps and selection candidates one step. Among military prestige titles, Champion Great General, commissioners-with-wafer, and military commissioners returning to service were reassigned to Roaming Strike General. Even when Central Secretariat clerks and agency clerks received such appointments, there was no cumulative-addition method; the rest were not routinely granted.
translations.idiomatic: On the civil prestige-rank tier, grace promotions added one step; on the Gentleman tier, capital and court officials received five steps and selection candidates one. Even Central Secretariat clerks and agency clerks who received such appointments had no cumulative-addition method; the rest were not routinely granted.
